items.title: Microsoft’s new AI ‘code of conduct’ tells models not to hack systems or trick humans
items.summary: The code of conduct lays out general principles that Microsoft AI models should uphold — supporting humans rather than replacing them, for instance, and accelerating human flourishing — as well as specific safety constraints meant to implement those principles.

items.title: How Fyxer built an AI executive assistant people trust
items.summary: Fyxer uses OpenAI models, fine-tuning, memory, and real user feedback to organize inboxes and draft emails in each user’s voice.

items.title: GitHub Copilot's Project HydraFusion Promises Frontier Level Performance through Multi-Model Routing
items.summary: GitHub's Project HydraFusion is a research preview for GitHub Copilot that enhances coding intelligence through runtime model orchestration. It dynamically assembles execution plans using models from various providers. The system employs three execution patterns based on task complexity. Evaluations indicate that it achieves high task quality while significantly reducing operational costs. By Olimpiu Pop

items.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
items.summary: Perplexity uses Astra to write communications, change software, and monitor production systems, and checks in much less frequently than with earlier models.

items.title: China fires back at U.S. AI safety warnings, calling them fearmongering to lock in American advantage
items.summary: China has flatly rejected warnings about AI risks from Anthropic CEO Amodei and other U.S. AI leaders. Beijing's Foreign Ministry calls it "fearmongering," while the state-run Global Times accuses Amodei of waging a "silent AI Cold War."
